issues.legal_issue: Municipal annual-value assessments of premises governed by rent control cannot exceed the fair rent determinable under the applicable rent-control law, even when a rent controller has not formally fixed the rent.
material_facts: The municipality revised rental values for tax assessment and increased some values beyond the fair rent determinable under the rent-control legislation.
The municipality argued that the rent-control limit applied only after a controller had formally fixed the fair rent.

The Court held that the same fair-rent measure applied whether or not the controller had fixed a rent; where no rent had been fixed, the municipality had to determine it using the statutory fair-rent principles.
issues.conclusion: A municipality may not assess premises above the fair rent determinable under the rent-control law, regardless of whether a rent controller has formally fixed that rent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 82(2) of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, measures annual value by the rent the premises may reasonably be expected to fetch, meaning rent lawfully obtainable from a hypothetical tenant. The municipality cannot use an arbitrary value and is bound by the fair or standard rent under the rent-control law. If no rent has been fixed by the controller, the municipality must determine fair rent by applying the principles in section 4 of the applicable Act. The Court followed Corporation of Calcutta v. Sm. Padma Debi & Ors. [1962] 3 S.C.R. 49.

rule.if: municipal_tax_assessment and premises_subject_to_rent_control and (fair_rent_formally_fixed or fair_rent_not_formally_fixed)

predicates.municipal_tax_assessment: A municipality is determining the taxable annual value of premises.
predicates.premises_subject_to_rent_control: The premises are governed by a rent-control regime that limits the rent lawfully obtainable for them.
predicates.fair_rent_formally_fixed: A rent controller has formally fixed the fair rent for the premises.
predicates.fair_rent_not_formally_fixed: A rent controller has not formally fixed the fair rent for the premises.

issues.definition: When a municipality assesses premises governed by rent control, whether or not a controller has formally fixed the rent, the assessment value cannot exceed the fair rent determinable for those premises.

issues.legal_issue: The rent-control law governing a municipal valuation is the law in force during the period for which the assessment is made.
material_facts: The municipal revision was made in 1960, after a new rent-control Act had come into force.
The lower courts relied on rent-control Acts that had been in force before the new Act.

The Court held that the fair rent for an earlier assessment period must be determined under the rent-control law then in force, and that the law in force during a later assessment period governs that period.
The assessment books were ordinarily revised every five years, but the applicable rules provided a procedure for changing an assessment when a case for change was made out.
issues.conclusion: A municipal valuation must be determined in accordance with the rent-control law in force during the period of assessment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 82(2) of the Madras District Municipalities Act, 1920, requires valuation by reference to the rent lawfully obtainable, and the applicable fair-rent measure is supplied by the rent-control law in force during the assessment period. Although the Fourth Schedule rules provided for quinquennial revision of assessment books, they also provided a procedure for changing assessments when warranted. The Court relied on the principle in Corporation of Calcutta v. Sm. Padma Debi & Ors. [1962] 3 S.C.R. 49.

predicates.municipal_tax_assessment: A municipality is determining the taxable annual value of premises.
predicates.assessment_period_has_rent_control_law: A rent-control law governs the period for which the municipal valuation is being assessed.

issues.definition: For a municipal tax assessment made for a period governed by rent-control law, the assessment must apply the rent-control law in force during that period.
